events.title: Egyptian New Kingdom rule in Nubia
hints: Pharaohs of the 18th dynasty pushed south beyond the Second Cataract after about 1500 BCE.
Viceroys known as King's Sons of Kush governed the region for centuries.
Gold mines and tribute from the south financed temples and campaigns.
events.summary: From around 1500 BCE the pharaohs of the New Kingdom conquered Nubia as far as the Fourth Cataract and administered it through a viceroy. Gold, cattle and labour flowed north, and Egyptian control ended around 1070 BCE.

events.title: Turco-Egyptian rule
hints: A ruler's army invaded from the north in 1820, seeking gold and enslaved soldiers.
A system of slave raids supplied soldiers, domestic servants and exports.
An Islamic uprising led by a self-proclaimed Mahdi overthrew it in 1885.
events.summary: Muhammad Ali Pasha's forces invaded in 1820 and the new government organised raids for slaves, ivory and gold, using enslaved men as soldiers. Taxation and the suppression of the slave trade under British pressure fuelled the Mahdist revolt, which captured Khartoum in 1885.

events.title: Anglo-Egyptian reconquest
hints: A British-led army advanced up the Nile from 1896 to avenge a general killed at Khartoum.
At Omdurman in September 1898, machine guns and artillery killed about 10,000 defenders.
A dual-flag arrangement was agreed in January 1899.
events.summary: Under General Kitchener, an Anglo-Egyptian army reconquered the territory from the Mahdist state between 1896 and 1898. At the Battle of Omdurman in September 1898 an estimated 10,000 Mahdist soldiers were killed against about 50 on the British side.

events.title: Anglo-Egyptian Sudan
hints: A nominal partnership in 1899 gave Britain effective control of a vast territory.
The north and south were administered separately, and a huge irrigation scheme grew cotton for Lancashire.
events.summary: The 1899 condominium agreement gave Britain and Egypt joint rule, with Britain in practice in charge. The Gezira Scheme from 1925 grew long-staple cotton for British mills, and the north and south were administered separately. Independence came on 1 January 1956.
